docs.hero.title: One endpoint. One key. Start building.
docs.hero.description: Connect SDKs and coding agents to a unified, OpenAI-compatible gateway with concise setup instructions you can copy and run.
docs.overview.capabilityEndpoint.title: Unified endpoint
docs.overview.capabilityEndpoint.descrip: Use one base URL across supported clients.
docs.overview.capabilityKey.title: Bearer authentication
docs.overview.capabilityKey.description: Use one uniRouters API key for every request.
docs.overview.capabilityProtocol.title: Multiple protocols
docs.overview.capabilityProtocol.descrip: Responses, Chat Completions, and Claude Messages.
docs.quickStart.title: From key to first response in minutes
docs.quickStart.description: Create a key in the Console, point your client at uniRouters, and keep the rest of your OpenAI-compatible integration unchanged.
docs.quickStart.stepKey.title: Create an API key
docs.quickStart.stepKey.description: Open Console → API Keys and create a key for your application.
docs.quickStart.stepBaseUrl.title: Set the base URL
docs.quickStart.stepBaseUrl.description: Point your SDK or agent to https://unirouters.cc/v1.
docs.quickStart.stepRequest.title: Send a request
docs.quickStart.stepRequest.description: Start with the Responses API and an available model.
docs.authentication.title: Authentication
docs.authentication.description: Pass your uniRouters key as a Bearer token on every API request. SDKs can read it from an environment variable.
docs.authentication.securityDescription: Never expose an API key in browser code, public repositories, screenshots, or support messages. Rotate it immediately if it leaks.
docs.sdks.title: OpenAI-compatible SDKs
docs.sdks.description: Existing OpenAI SDK integrations usually need only two changes: the base URL and API key.
docs.agents.title: Coding agents
docs.agents.description: Route supported coding agents through uniRouters while keeping credentials in environment variables.
docs.agents.codex.title: Codex CLI
docs.agents.codex.description: Export your uniRouters key, then add a custom Responses API provider to your user-level Codex config.
docs.agents.claudeCode.title: Claude Code
docs.agents.claudeCode.description: Set the gateway origin, Bearer token, and an available uniRouters model before starting Claude Code.
docs.agents.claudeCode.baseUrlNote: Claude Code appends /v1/messages itself, so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL uses https://unirouters.cc without /v1.
docs.reference.title: API reference
docs.reference.description: Choose the protocol your client already supports. Model and feature availability can vary; check the Model Square before integrating.
docs.reference.responses.title: Responses API
docs.reference.responses.description: Recommended for Codex and agentic workflows with streaming and tool use.
docs.reference.chat.title: Chat Completions
docs.reference.chat.description: For OpenAI-compatible chat clients and existing integrations.
docs.reference.messages.title: Claude Messages
docs.reference.messages.description: Anthropic-format endpoint used by Claude Code and compatible clients.
docs.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
docs.troubleshooting.description: Most setup issues can be isolated by checking the status code, base URL, key, and model name.
docs.troubleshooting.401.title: Invalid or missing key
docs.troubleshooting.401.description: Confirm the key is active and sent as a Bearer token without extra spaces or quotes.
docs.troubleshooting.429.title: Rate or concurrency limit reached
docs.troubleshooting.429.description: Reduce parallel requests, add exponential backoff, and retry after the indicated delay.
docs.troubleshooting.5xx.title: Upstream temporarily unavailable
docs.troubleshooting.5xx.description: Retry idempotent requests with backoff. If it persists, try another available model.
docs.troubleshooting.supportDescription: include the HTTP status, request ID, model name, endpoint, and UTC time. Never include the full API key.
